survey: A 3D-rendered park chess set on grass with a cream path and trees behind it. It has three parts. (1) The table: a thick square slab with rounded edges, seen from above at a three-quarter angle. The chessboard pattern is printed on its top face. (2) The table's support: a square column in the middle of the slab's underside, standing on a wider square plinth that lies flat on the grass and casts a shadow. (3) Two round stools: one back-left, one front-right. Each is a cylinder with a wider rounded cap, and each stands upright on the grass with its own contact shadow. The checker squares shrink and bunch up toward the far edge of the board, and their rows run parallel to the slab's edges. The slab, column and plinth turn the same way. The plinth's edges are steeper than the slab's because it sits lower, below eye level, which is what one camera would show. The column's verticals stay vertical. The stool tops are true ellipses. The nearer, lower right stool's ellipse is slightly rounder than the farther left one's, which also fits one camera. Everything meets the ground at the ground's angle. The board's light and dark squares are not evenly placed, but that is a pattern issue, not perspective.
